title: composition.json
description: Declarative scene-graph for one frame (start or end) of a shot. Fed to compose_preview.py to render a layout blueprint, then to compose_blend.py to produce the final photoreal keyframe.

ref.description: Project-relative path to the base/background image (usually a location plate).

elements.description: Elements composited on top of the base, in z_order ascending. Positions are normalized 0.0-1.0 to the canvas; anchor is top-left of the element's bounding box.

id.description: Stable identifier — e.g. character id, prop slug.

ref.description: Project-relative path to the element's reference image (turnaround, wardrobe variant, prop detail, etc.).

width.description: Width relative to canvas. Values > 1 are allowed for close-ups that crop into the element.

z_order.description: Lower = further back. Used for preview stacking AND communicated to the blender.

pose_hint.description: Natural-language pose/expression direction fed into the blend prompt. E.g. 'crouched, hands cupping the lamp, eyes closed'.

motion_intent.description: Only filled for the END frame. Describes what changes between start and end so the video model interpolates correctly.

summary.description: One sentence — e.g. 'Elias rises to standing, turns head toward the window'.

camera_move.description: Redundant with shots.json but useful for the blender to frame the end correctly.

blend_prompt.description: Natural-language direction for the blender. Tells it to photorealistically composite per the blueprint, preserving identity of each element from its ref image.

negative_prompt.description: What to avoid (e.g. 'no duplicate characters, no text, no watermark').
